paper_title: A Neural Network-Evolutionary Computation Framework for Remaining Useful Life Estimation
core_problem: Estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of mechanical systems efficiently, addressing the time-consuming nature of tuning data-related parameters in traditional methods.
methodology_summary: A framework combining a multi-layer perceptron (neural network) with an evolutionary algorithm for optimizing data-related parameters. It uses a strided time window and automatically reshapes data to increase model efficiency while maintaining low complexity (few hidden layers/neurons).
empirical_results: The proposed method's accuracy is compared against other state-of-the-art methods on the C-MAPSS dataset. Good prognostics results have been achieved, though data-driven approaches typically have wider confidence intervals than model-based approaches.
explicit_limitations: The current study uses specific regressors and evolutionary algorithms; the framework's generality allows for other combinations. Future work will extend the framework for model selection and analyze the influence of the window stride parameter (ns).
pipeline_steps: The framework presented here automatically reshapes the data such that the efficiency of the model is increased.
